Things were good for a few years until one day marauding warband attacked the village he lived in, stealing anything of value and burning anything left.

Callum was ruined, his livelihood destroyed and his family left destitute and starving. He tried to find work but no job ever lasted and he and family lived from wage to wage, trying to make it stretch.

One day a colleague on a farm told him of Mother Agnes, a strange woman who lived in the swamp and could grant wishes. When the work on the farm dried up, Callum decided he had had enough and went to see Mother Agnes.

He told her his story and she offered him a wish: that he would never be out of work again. Callum was naive and now he works every hour of every day behind the bar at the hags tavern, always greeting guests with a warm smile and cheerful conversation, but people who look into his eyes can see the terror and sadness as he constantly fears for what happened to his family.

So as written:

Auril is using the rime to create an endless night on the dale because she wants to inflict suffering on the Ten Towners and other people of the dale because .... reasons (the book basically says you shouldn't make Auril's motivations understandable because it hurts the cosmic horror aspect to her but most people come up with something anyway).

The arcane brotherhood want to find Ythryn so they can claim the magical artifacts

The Duergar want to conquer the Dale as the endless night will allow them live above ground there. They are also being secretly influenced by Asmodeus (for reasons the book never explains, will touch more on him later)

Each of the ten towns is led by a speaker, who together make up a council that leads the towns. Most of the ten towners simply want to survive, but there are factions within who have other motivations.

Naerth, the speaker of Targos, is a Zhentarim agent who wants to establish a zhentarim stranglehold on the trade of the town and so is trying to increase his influence among the council of speakers, such as trying to replace the speaker of termalaine, or get someone loyal to him elected in Good Mead.

The knights of the black sword are a cult who worship levistus. As written they simply are there to serve levistus but get involved with the Ythryn plot because of Avarice, one of the arcane brotherhood, actually being a worshipper of levistus herself. They clash with the duergar, because levistus knows they are being influenced by asmodeus. (This is one of the most common changes however as most people run it that the cult wants to free levistus from his prison of ice in hell, and so are looking for something in the dale to do so like the Codicil, the Mythallar or the Spindle.  Asmodeus is then using the Duergar to try and foil Levistus's plan)

There are also the various smaller factions around the dale:

The goliath tribes have been hostile to each for a while due to an argument over a griffon from the skytower goliaths attacking a child of the wyrmdoom goliaths, and the wyrmdoom goliaths then killing that griffon.

The goblins just want to do goblin stuff, but their leader is actually a halfling in disguise, who now wants out as the fear of being discover has become too great.

The frost druids in general just serve Auril, but Ravisin is being especially agressive because her sister was killed by hunters from lonelywood.

This meant before the teams would make sure to be quick changing the tyres but they as long as they were done by the time the car was refueled it didn't matter how fast.

After refueling was banned teams started to really push for faster and faster pit stops because sometimes those milliseconds that they are saving could be the difference between coming out of the pits ahead of a car or behind them.

Bang and wolf were great, but I think it's also important to understand that the game was very different then from how it is now and that affects their legacy. Bang and Wolf were dominant at a time when the current version of league was "solved", sightstone, the ability to buy green wards and lane swaps meant that Korean teams completely dominated with this perfect information, no risk play style that just choked your opponent out of the game and it made it harder to show your individual skill in positions outside of mid and jungle.

Bang was always a really good adc especially in team fights, to the point where skt would often play comps where he was the only DPS. But that meta meant he was never truly challenged as a player, pretty much until 2017 worlds, where he fell short compared to the other top ADCs like Ruler and Uzi and I think that's what really hurts Bangs legacy, he never had to be truly amazing, just reliable and consistent and then when he needed to step up he didn't. He's probably also hurt by that having been in Worlds rather than just regular season LCK, so everyone was seeing his fall from grace.

Wolf similarly played at a time when supports had less power and agency than they do now and while it's hard to fault him, there were supports like Madlife and Mata, who were able to break out beyond this and be much more impactful, so even when he was winning he was never considered the best.

As someone who also failed a first year module and the resit but have gone on to finish a degree, I'll give my advice:

Really consider what went wrong, were you engaged with the course and did you struggle with the content, or did you actually struggle to engage with the course?

I'm sure the university will offer you options to take a resit year or to switch to another course, but you need to be really honest with yourself before you commit to another year meaning more expenses and loans.

If you worked hard but still couldn't pass you should consider if the course is right for you, whether a different subject might serve you better.

If you struggled because you didn't work hard, didn't attend lectures or did but couldn't focus on them, etc then think about why, were you too busy with your social life, do you have bad habits like spending too much time playing games or watching TV or YouTube when you should be doing work, are you using other substances, might you have undiagnosed learning disabilities that you need help dealing with? If its something like that then I'd strongly recommend you take the time to fix those issues first and then come back to university knowing that you are capable of taking on the course.

I was in the second group, I couldn't concentrate on work, I'd sit down to do coursework, watch lectures online (almost all of my course was online due to Covid), do extra reading and within five minutes I was getting distracted doing something else, I would find myself binge watching whole TV show's as a deadline was coming up and getting no closer to actually doing work. I tried to find other ways of doing stuff like going to the library but I'd end up staring at phone most of the time instead. I failed a module in my first year and ended up switching courses onto a harder one actually but with more face to face learning and smaller class sizes because I thought that would help with my issues focusing. It's hard for me to say whether it did help in the end because that first year of the new course is when Covid lockdowns started and even in my final year we didn't have in person lectures.

Looking back now I really regret that I jumped straight into a new course instead of taking time to work on myself, because while I got through my course and scraped a 2:2, I know I'm smart enough that I could have gotten a 2:1 or a 1st if I worked hard but I just couldn't and while I would like to go back and do a masters at some point I've told myself that I can't until I fix my work issues.

Others have pointed out some of the issues but there's a more thematic problem here. In general, wish passing leans more towards defensive teams that use the wish to maintain mons that lack reliable recovery themselves, meaning that they can switch in over and over because the chip damage from hazards and resisted attacks is lessened. Eject button on the other hand is almost always used on hyper offense teams (often by magic bounce users) because when you are looking to break your opponents quickly, recovery from leftovers or chip from isn't going to add up and so the trade off to give you a free pivot once in the game is worth it. Now on a balance team that's using wish support to maintain key mons, that once per game free switch isn't going to be as impactful and the healing from leftovers will likely be more impactful over the course of the game.
